harpreet: FYI onboarding pegasus-liteq. funcall conformance failing in streaming only; parsing errors look like broken string literals across chunk boundaries. non-streaming ok.

mike_t: can you paste a raw chunk sequence?

harpreet: sure. raw assembler chunks below (showing byte escapes):
chunk A: '{"action":"search","args":{"q":"Find restaurants with
'
chunk B: ' outdoor seating","filters":[]}}'
When concatenated naively we get an embedded \n in the middle of the JSON string which some parsers accept (escaped) and others see as an actual newline token, causing parse failure.

gloria: interesting edge-case. escaped newlines should be two bytes \\n but runtime is emitting literal newline bytes across a chunk boundary. Likely a tokeniser/decoder mismatch in liteq emitter where escapes are not normalized.

qa-bot: repro harness available: python tests/stream_escape_repro.py --model pegasus-liteq --seed 1337 --requests 8000 --streaming -> reproduces ~1.3% broken-string failures.

mike_t: quick mitigations? sanitizer that collapses raw control LF inside quotes into \\n before parse? risky as it mutates user content.

harpreet: alternatives: 1) chunk-aware string repair: detect odd-number-of-quote parity across boundary and if inside string, join next chunk into buffer and escape real newlines, 2) boundary-check heuristic: keep last 64 bytes, compute quote parity and backslash-escape parity to detect cut inside escape sequence, 3) fallback NDJSON-wrap / repair attempts.

gloria: implement heuristic first: on streaming assembler, if first non-whitespace char of next chunk is not '{' or '[' and last chunk ends with an unclosed quote -> buffer until either we see closing quote or max_buffer_ms reached. Emit metric parse.buffered_string_fragments.

mike_t: add flag --stream-escape-buffer-ms (default 0). Also expose metric parse.string_repair_attempts and parse.string_repair_success.

qa-bot: tests to add: unit for quote/backslash parity checker, integration that simulates random split across escape sequences, and an eval that replays 5k previously-failed streams to compare tool.exec divergence.

harpreet: important: don't transform payload content unless repair succeeded deterministically. We'll record every repaired payload to internal bucket for audit. Limit repairs per request to 1 and max_buffer_bytes=2048.

ci-bot: PR created: #4987 pegasus-liteq streaming escape-buffer + metrics (https://git.internal/r/4987). CI build passed.

mike_t: rollout plan: 1) merge behind flag, 2) dogfood on small dedicated pool, 3) measure parse.string_repair_success vs schema.fail_rate and tool.exec divergence, 4) decide default.

gloria: one more thought: add a tokenizer-level sentinel check: emit a small token parity checksum in runtime when streaming (opt-in) so assembler can cheaply know safe cutpoints. Longer-term fix but requires runtime changes.

harpreet: will coordinate with runtime team for sentinel plan. For now I'll land assembler flag and tests. Dogfood tomorrow morning.

mike_t: thanks, please paste dogfood metrics in this thread. :thumbsup:

harpreet: will do.
